subject: Dedicated GPU pool sizing: latency SLAs, stress test plan & decision log
messages:
From: Emily Park <emily.park@lumenedge.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: ops@lumenedge.com
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: LumenEdge RFP — dedicated pool sizing and acceptance criteria

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the RFP intake yesterday. Two follow-ups from our infra/procurement teams as we map internal acceptance criteria for a dedicated pool:

- Baseline workloads: a conversational chat model (approx 6k tokens/session, avg 12 requests/min during peak) and an embeddings pipeline (batch embed jobs, 8k vectors per job).
- Latency SLOs: p95 <= 250ms for chat streaming segments, p99 <= 1.5s for end-to-end generation (including network). For embeddings we want <= 120ms per vector on average when batched.
- Peak concurrency window: expected 3x baseline for 30-minute bursts, sustained 1.2x for business hours.
- Concern: we need a documented stress-test plan (tooling, acceptance gates, pass/fail criteria) and a recommended GPU mix (H100 vs A100 vs mixed with L4 for embeddings) that balances cost and tail-latency.

Can you send a short stress-test plan + a decision rationale for GPU selection and fallback policies? Also include any kernels/quantization constraints we should put in the RFP. I attached our workload_profile.json in case it helps.

Best,
Emily Park
Director, Platform Engineering
LumenEdge

Attachment: lumenedge_workload_profile.json (stub)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Emily Park <emily.park@lumenedge.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: LumenEdge RFP — dedicated pool sizing and acceptance criteria

Emily — thanks, this is very helpful.

Summary (quick): yes — we can meet your SLOs with multiple GPU mixes; the trade-offs are cost vs. tail-latency headroom and warm-cache requirements. I attached a workbook that models throughput, slotting, and estimated committed units for three scenarios: "Latency-First" (H100 heavy), "Cost-Balanced" (A100 primary + L4 embedters), and "Elastic-Hybrid" (commit with burst lane + on-demand fallback).

High-level recommended approach:
- Start with A100_80GB primary for conversation workloads (good balance for long contexts) and L4 instances for high-volume embedding batches.
- If your p99 tail is stricter than 1.5s under real traffic, shift to H100_80GB for the critical subset of routes (chat-highprio).
- Enable prefix KV caching and a warmup runway (30–60s) for session-heavy flows — helps p95 by ~20–30% in our evals.
- Quantization: use int8/Q4_0 for most embedding models; for chat generative models prefer FP16 unless model accuracy regressions observed.

Stress-test plan (attached summary + workbook):
- Load generator: phased test (ramp to 1x, 3x, 5x baseline) with synthetic sessions that mimic token distributions in your workload_profile.json.
- Acceptance gates: p95 under target at 3x baseline; p99 not exceeding 1.5s for critical routes; embedding throughput within 10% of modelled batch baseline.
- Safety checks: kernel-fitment sanity (see kernel_fitment_matrix.csv), cold-start amplification checks, cache hit-rate targets (>= 65% warm prefix for conversational flows).

Next steps:
1) We (Redwood) will share: redwood_capacity_workbook_LUM_v3.xlsx (attached), stress_plan_runbook.pdf, and kernel_fitment_matrix.csv.
2) Review and confirm which routes are "critical" for H100 vs A100.
3) We schedule a 60-minute stress-run (lab) with your SREs — propose Thurs 11/05 10:00–11:00 PT.

I'll wait for confirmation and any procurement contacts to include in the DocuSign drafts.

— Karthik Iyer
Sr. Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0126

Attachments: redwood_capacity_workbook_LUM_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: LumenEdge RFP — stress-run specifics and kernel fitment notes (internal)

Internal notes / proposed runbook details — posting here so we have a decision log:

1) GPU mix rationale (short):
   - H100_80GB: best for extremely long-context or large-batch attention kernels (chat with 6k tokens). Reduces number of cross-stream kernel launches and keeps tail-latency low at high concurrency. Cost premium ~1.4x vs A100.
   - A100_80GB: our default recommendation for balanced workloads; good density for most LLMs at variable sequence lengths.
   - L4 family: cost-effective for embedding-only routes; pair with batching windows of 250–500ms to hit per-vector latency targets.

2) Stress-test acceptance gates (concrete):
   - Gate A (Functional): end-to-end success rate >= 99.5% at 3x baseline for 30 minutes.
   - Gate B (Latency): p95 streaming segment <= 250ms; p99 end-to-end <= 1.5s for critical chat routes. For embedding batches, mean per-vector <= 120ms when batching at 256 vectors.
   - Gate C (Stability): no more than 2 retries triggered by KV cache misses during the 30-minute window; no more than 5% error increase over baseline.

3) Runbook highlights (attachments): stress_plan_runbook.pdf contains:
   - Stepwise ramp (0.5x, 1x, 3x, 5x), warm vs cold runs, observation windows.
   - Exact metrics to capture: token-emit latencies, kernel queue lengths, GPU occupancy, NVLink transfer rates, preemption events.
   - Fallback playbook: automatic model-variant fallback -> cross-region paired pool -> short-duration burst from on-demand pool.

4) Kernel-fitment: see kernel_fitment_matrix.csv for model->kernel recommendations and quantization compatibility. We should flag models with custom operators (will require a compatibility run).

Questions for Karthik before stress run scheduling:
- Confirm critical route list (we need explicit paths/route names for canary pinning).
- Does LumenEdge allow a short maintenance window that permits transient autoscaling during the test (helps with realistic tail-latency behavior)?

I'll prepare the stress-run CI job and parameter templates once we confirm routes.

— Jonas Weber
Senior Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference
